answer: Demand-side scarcity caps throughput to match verifier capacity. The protocol raises a dynamic base fee as the queue deepens; attackers must harbor ever-increasing capital just to enter. Each epoch builds a trellis of fee-burned transactions where honest agents amortize costs while clone armies pay per head. On the terrace of congestion, the fee exceeds any sybil budget, and hard block limits enforce scarcity. One honest agent pays once; a thousand clones pay a thousand times.
